note: Curated image and photo applications. Every entry is reviewed by hand; nothing here is discovered, fetched or promoted automatically. The 'differences' field is written by the curator and is the only place a comparison between options may come from.

entries.name: Bunny Image Tool
entries.purpose: Make a smaller copy of an image, without opening anything.

permissionReasons.files: to read the image you chose and write the smaller copy

entries.differences: Ships with Bunny OS and does one thing: a scaled copy of an image, at the width you asked for, saved beside the original. It has no window and no settings. GIMP and Krita are the editors; this is what Bunny reaches for when you only want a smaller copy, because it needs nothing installed and it never touches the file you gave it.

entries.name: GIMP
entries.purpose: Edit photographs and images: retouch, cut out, adjust colour, work in layers.

permissionReasons.files: to open the image you choose and save the result
permissionReasons.folders: to work through a folder of images in one go
permissionReasons.gpu: to make large images respond while you edit them
permissionReasons.notifications: to tell you when a long export has finished

entries.differences: Does most of what a commercial photo editor does, including layers, masks and colour work. It does not open Photoshop's PSD files perfectly — text layers and some adjustment layers come in flattened — and it has no cloud library, no subscription-only filters and no support desk. The interface is arranged differently and takes a while to learn if you know Photoshop.

entries.name: Krita
entries.purpose: Paint and draw: digital painting, illustration, concept art.

permissionReasons.files: to open and save the picture you are working on
permissionReasons.folders: to keep a project's files together
permissionReasons.gpu: to keep brushes responsive on a large canvas

entries.differences: Built for painting rather than for photo editing. Brush engines are its strength; it is a poor choice for retouching a photograph or laying out a page. Reads PSD files better than most, writes them adequately.

entries.name: Adobe Photoshop
entries.purpose: The commercial standard for photo editing and compositing.
entries.sandboxNote: Adobe does not publish a Linux build. Bunny cannot install it, cannot put it in a capsule and cannot promise anything about it. It is listed so you know it exists and what it would cost.
entries.differences: The reference product. Best PSD support, best commercial plug-in ecosystem, subscription-only, requires an Adobe account, and has no Linux version at all — so on this computer it is not an option Bunny can offer, only one it can tell you about.

entries.name: Photopea
entries.purpose: Photoshop-like image editing in a browser tab.
entries.sandboxNote: This runs in a web page, so the isolation is the browser's rather than Bunny's, and Bunny cannot tell you what happens to a file after you upload it.
entries.differences: Opens PSD files well and is free to use with adverts. Your image goes to a web page rather than staying on this computer, which is the difference that matters if the picture is private.

entries.name: ImageMagick
entries.purpose: Convert, resize and batch-process images without a window.

permissionReasons.files: to read the image you named and write the converted one
permissionReasons.folders: to convert a whole folder at once

entries.differences: Has no window at all — Bunny drives it for you. Excellent at conversion, resizing and simple batch work; it cannot do the interactive editing GIMP and Krita are for, and its background removal is a colour-key rather than the subject detection a photo editor does.
